कोई आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड नहीं मिला. हालांकि, न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री को मिले वीडियो में उसी दिन गाड़ी में सवार एक व्यक्ति को उसी गाड़ी से लाठियां निकालते हुए देखा गया. यह वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर भी वायरल हुआ. हमने इन युवाओं के बारे में पड़ताल की. हमने पाया कि गाड़ी के आसपास मौजूद लोग एक ऐसे समूह का हिस्सा थे, जिसके सदस्य पहले भी खुले तौर पर प्रदर्शनकारियों के खिलाफ बल प्रयोग करने की मांग कर चुके थे और कुछ मौकों पर हिंसा में भी शामिल रहे थे. यह वही समूह है, जिसके सदस्यों को सप्ताहांत में प्रदर्शनकारियों और पत्रकारों के मुकाबले पुलिस की उतनी सख्त जांच-पड़ताल का सामना करते नहीं देखा गया. जब हम यह स्टोरी कर रहे थे तो पुलिस के साथ साथ पुलिस के साथ मौजूद, जो कि खुद को राष्ट्रवादी बता रहे थे, उन्होंने मुझे कई बार हैकल किया. हैरानी कि बात यह कि पुलिस भी वहां मौजूद थी. ये लोग सिर्फ मुझे हैकल नहीं कर रहे थे बल्कि वहां पर आने वाले प्रदर्शनकारियों के साथ भी उलझ रहे थे. और उन्हें पुलिस के हवाले कर रहे थे. ऐसा लग रहा था जैसे ये लोग पुलिस के फ्रंट के तौर पर काम कर रहे हों. और ऐसा कई घंटों तक चलता रहा. ये लोग पहले प्रदर्शनकारियों को पीटते.. फिर पुलिस के हवाले करते और पुलिस इन्हें डिटेन कर बस से ले जाती. यहां साफ दिखाई दे रहा था कि पुलिस उनके साथ मिलकर काम कर रही थी. इनकी जुगलबंदी की हर तस्वीर को हम डॉक्यूमेंट कर रहे थे. फिर शाम के करीब पांच बजे जब पुलिस को लगा कि हम सब रिकॉर्ड कर रहे हैं तो इस दौरान ही पुलिस हमारे सामने आकर खड़ी हो गई. ताकि हम यह सब रिकॉर्ड ना कर पाएं. अब सवाल यह है कि पुलिस की मौजूदगी में ये लोग इतनी बेखौफ़ होकर हिंसा कैसे करते रहे? और जब बार-बार गाड़ी की जांच की मांग होती रही, तो उसे रोकने के बजाय मौके से घेराबंदी कर क्यों हटाया गया. इन सवालों के जवाब मिलने ज़रूरी हैं. ये पूरा वीडियो देखिए और पुलिस के साथ स्वघोषित राष्ट्रवादी कर रहे थे उसे समझिए- प्रदर्शनकारियों को दौड़ाती और फिर पकड़ती दिल्ली पुलिस, कनॉट प्लेस पर दिनभर चली पकड़-धकड़ जंतर-मंतर प्रदर्शन: दिल्ली पुलिस की घेराबंदी से हिरासत तक, दिनभर का पूरा हाल ‘लिखकर दो कि दिल्ली नहीं जाओगे’: जंतर-मंतर प्रदर्शन से पहले गुजरात में पुलिस की कार्रवाई

items.title: एनएल चर्चा 445: पत्रकारों और प्रदर्शनकारियों की धरपकड़ के बीच एंटी-SIR आंदोलन का भविष्य, क्या एक मंच पर आ पाएगा विपक्ष?
items.summary: एनएल चर्चा के इस अंक में मुख्य रूप से स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिविज़न और मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ चल रहे विरोध प्रदर्शनों, दिल्ली पुलिस द्वारा मीडिया कवरेज के दौरान 30 से अधिक पत्रकारों की गिरफ्तारी व पुलिसिया दमन और विपक्ष द्वारा 'वोट चोरी' के खिलाफ एकजुट होकर आंदोलन करने पर विस्तार से चर्चा की गई. इसके साथ ही कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी द्वारा कनॉट प्लेस के सेंट्रल पार्क में आयोजित 'तिरंगा मार्च', गृह मंत्री अमित शाह द्वारा राहुल गांधी पर 'घुसपैठियों को बचाने' का आरोप, और अभिनेता इमरान खान को मुंबई छोड़ने के पुलिसिया नोटिस पर भी विस्तृत बातचीत हुई. वहीं, बिहार के वैशाली जिले में गंडक-गंगा नदी में नाव पलटने से 13 बच्चों की मौत, मेरठ के चर्चित 'ब्लू ड्रम' हत्याकांड में अदालत द्वारा पत्नी और प्रेमी को फांसी की सजा, केंद्रीय राज्य मंत्री एल. मुरुगन का इस्तीफा, भारत-चीन व्यापार घाटा पहली बार 100 अरब डॉलर के पार पहुंचना, एयर इंडिया की फ्रैंकफर्ट-दिल्ली फ्लाइट में 'हाइजैक 7500' कोड के कारण जयपुर डायवर्जन का भ्रम, मध्य प्रदेश के सिवनी जिला अस्पताल में 6 महीने के भीतर 80 नवजातों की मौत पर बवाल और बांग्लादेश की पूर्व पीएम शेख हसीना द्वारा ब्रिक्स सम्मेलन में न जाने पर अंतरिम सरकार के फैसले की आलोचना आदि ख़बरें भी हफ्ते भर चर्चा में रहे. इस हफ्ते न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री टीम से अवधेश कुमार, अनमोल प्रितम और आकांख्या राउत ने चर्चा में हिस्सा लिया. चर्चा का संचालन वरिष्ठ पत्रकार हृदयेश जोशी और न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री की प्रमुख संपादक मनीषा पांडे ने किया. चर्चा की शुरुआत करते हुए मनीषा कहती हैं, “10 अक्टूबर को जो प्रोटेस्ट की योजना थी वह तो सफल नहीं हो पाती है लेकिन हम पहली बार दिल्ली में इतनी फ़ोर्स देखते हैं और शाम होते होते सात हज़ार लोग हिरासत में ले लिए जाते हैं जिसमें 30 पत्रकार थे. पत्रकारों के लिए हिरासत नई बात नहीं है लेकिन इतने बड़े पैमाने पर और धड़ल्ले से लोगों को डिटेन किया गया यह पहली बार शायद दिल्ली में हुआ होगा.” इस विषय पर अनमोल कहते हैं, “20 जुलाई वाला जो प्रोटेस्ट था, उस समय भी पत्रकारों को पुलिस की लाठियां पड़ी थीं लेकिन वह यह था कि पुलिस प्रदर्शनकारियों पर कार्रवाई कर रही है कोई बीच में पड़ गया लेकिन पत्रकारों को टारगेट करके नहीं मारा गया. इसके विपरीत 10 अक्टूबर बार वाली कार्रवाई अलग थी सुबह से ही पुलिस ने तय कर दिया था कि मीडिया यहीं से कवर करेगी और यह बेहद मुश्किल था उन पत्रकारों के लिए जो मोबाइल से शूट कर रहे थे. साथ ही सुरक्षा बलों को स्पष्ट निर्देश थे कि कोई भी बीच में आए तो उसे हिरासत में ले लिया जाए चाहे वह कोई यूट्यूबर हो, इन्फ्लुएंसर हो या पत्रकार.” सुनिए पूरी चर्चा - टाइमकोड्स: 00:00 - इंट्रो और ज़रूरी सूचना 5:56 - सुर्खियां 07:45 - items.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke released on bail; told to sign a one-year peace bond
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, who was placed under preventive arrest by the Delhi Police on October 16, was released on bail today following an order by a special executive magistrate in Delhi, according to LiveLaw . Dipke was detained that evening as he tried to make his way to Connaught Place to participate in the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest called by the CJP at Central Park. The conditions of his bail are not yet clear, but according to LiveLaw , he has been asked to sign a peace bond requiring him to maintain peace and public tranquillity for a year, as stated under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). Section 126 empowers an executive magistrate to take preventive action against anyone likely to cause a breach of the peace or a public disturbance. According to the police, they initiated action under Sections 126 and 170 (preventive arrest without a warrant or a magistrate’s order) of the BNSS against Dipke. Neha Bora, who was also detained that evening while she was marching from Mandi House, was released earlier today. Meanwhile, other CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in judicial custody . Delhi Police detained and then arrested them after they tried to enter the Jantar Mantar area on October 13, according to Bar and Bench . Complaining about the media is easy. items.title: हृदयेश जोशी को कुलदीप नैयर पत्रकारिता सम्मान, स्वतंत्र और तथ्यपरक पत्रकारिता में तीन दशक का योगदान
items.summary: वरिष्ठ स्वतंत्र पत्रकार और न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री के सहयोगी हृदयेश जोशी को वर्ष 2024 के लिए कुलदीप नैयर पत्रकारिता सम्मान से सम्मानित किया जाएगा. गांधी शांति प्रतिष्ठान ने 16 अक्टूबर 2026 को नई दिल्ली में आयोजित प्रेस वार्ता में इसकी घोषणा की. यह सम्मान स्वतंत्र, तथ्यपरक और प्रगतिशील पत्रकारिता के क्षेत्र में उल्लेखनीय योगदान देने वाले पत्रकारों को दिया जाता है. सम्मान के तहत एक लाख रुपये की राशि, प्रशस्ति-पत्र और प्रतीक चिह्न दिया जाता है. हृदयेश जोशी के साथ वर्ष 2025 के पुरस्कार के लिए पत्रकार श्याम मीरा सिंह को भी चुना गया है. दोनों को 24 अक्टूबर को गांधी शांति प्रतिष्ठान के सभागार में सम्मानित किया जाएगा. हृदयेश जोशी करीब तीन दशक से पत्रकारिता में सक्रिय हैं. उन्होंने पर्यावरण संबंधित पत्रकारिता में विशेष योगदान दिया. उनकी पत्रकारिता में पर्यावरण, राजनीति और समाज से जुड़े सवालों पर खास ध्यान रहा है. उन्होंने इन विषयों को आम लोगों के बीच पहुंचाने के साथ-साथ उन पर गंभीर चर्चा को भी जगह दी है. पर्यावरण से जुड़े मुद्दों पर जोशी के काम को खास पहचान मिली है. उन्होंने पर्यावरण और विकास से जुड़े सवालों पर लिखा है और अपनी रिपोर्टिंग के जरिए इन मुद्दों को सामने रखा है. वह पर्यावरण से जुड़े विषयों पर कई किताबों का अनुवाद भी कर चुके हैं. उनके काम में पर्यावरण संरक्षण और विकास के बीच के सवालों को समझने की कोशिश दिखाई देती है. जोशी ने अपनी पत्रकारिता के दौरान बदलते मीडिया के साथ भी खुद को जोड़े रखा है. उन्होंने प्रिंट और टेलीविजन के अलावा डिजिटल माध्यमों में भी काम किया है. वह न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री के लिए भी लगातार रिपोर्टिंग करते रहते हैं और यूट्यूब पर भी सक्रिय हैं. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री पर जोशी की रिपोर्टिंग पढ़ने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें. मालूम हो कि कुलदीप नैयर पत्रकारिता सम्मान की शुरुआत स्वतंत्र और प्रगतिशील पत्रकारिता को प्रोत्साहित करने के उद्देश्य से की गई थी. गांधी शांति प्रतिष्ठान और इससे जुड़े लोगों ने इस सम्मान की कल्पना की थी. दिवंगत पत्रकार कुलदीप नैयर ने भी इसके लिए आर्थिक सहयोग दिया था और दूसरों को योगदान देने के लिए प्रेरित किया था. सम्मान के जरिए ऐसी पत्रकारिता को पहचान देने की कोशिश की जाती है, जो तथ्यों, स्वतंत्र विचार और वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण को महत्व देती है. हृदयेश जोशी को यह सम्मान ऐसे समय में दिया जा रहा है, जब पत्रकारिता में पर्यावरण, राजनीति और सामाजिक सवालों पर गंभीर रिपोर्टिंग की जरूरत लगातार बनी हुई है. उनका चयन इन विषयों पर लंबे समय से किए जा रहे उनके काम को मिली पहचान है. उत्तरकाशी के धराली का सच क्या है, बादल फटा… या कुछ और? डॉक्यूमेंट्री: फूड चेन में आर्सेनिक और बिगड़ता सामाजिक तानाबाना ​आर्सेनिक डॉक्यूमेंट्री: बंगाल के विधवा गांव और items.title: Imran Khan moves Bombay High Court against FRRO's ‘Leave India’ notice; flags procedural lapses
items.summary: Bollywood actor Imran Khan has approached the Bombay High Court challenging the notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) which directs him to leave the country by October 28 for allegedly violating the Foreigners Act. [Imran Khan Pal v. Union of India & Ors] In his petition, Khan has contended that executive authorities gave him no prior hearing, bypassed his statutory rights as an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI), and acted in hasty response to political social media campaigns. The American national was directed by FRRO to leave the country by October 28. This was after he was briefly detained by the police after taking part in demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The directive was issued shortly after Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kirit Somaiya filed an FIR at the Gamdevi police station alleging public-order infractions under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. On October 17, FRRO issued a show cause notice asking Khan why his OCI registration should not be cancelled under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act. The plea is likely to be mentioned before a division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on October 19. Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna Grounds In the petition filed on October 17, Khan has challenged the FRRO order issued under Section 7(2)(c) read with Section 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act (IFA), 2025. According to the plea, Khan has lived in India for more than four decades with an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) registration since 2006. The plea also highlights the unusual haste in issuing the expulsion directive. Khan has alleged that authorities acted under pressure from public social media campaigns by political functionaries rather than an independent application of mind. items.title: NHRC: Who will keep the keeper?
items.summary: On October 12, as the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) marked its 33rd Foundation Day. Its Chairperson, Justice V Ramasubramanian, described the office of the Chief Justice of India as one put to an agni pariksha (trial by fire) every minute, and “not necessarily by sacred souls”. Chief Justice Surya Kant offered a line that deserves to outlive the occasion: if the Constitution is the promise, the Commission is one of its keepers. It is a fine line. It also raises an uncomfortable question. Who ensures that the keeper is fit to keep? The question is not academic. Between November 9 and 20, the Sub-Committee on Accreditation of the Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions (GANHRI) will decide whether the NHRC keeps the ‘A’ status it has held since 1999. In 2025, the Sub-Committee recommended a downgrade to ‘B’. The Commission’s challenge was rejected in December. The concerns on record are familiar: an opaque appointment process, thin pluralism and gender representation, the government’s power to post a senior civil servant as Secretary-General and police officers investigating complaints against the police. The Commission is entitled to answer each of these. But the answer will be judged by reform, not rhetoric. What would a downgrade cost? It would not trigger sanctions or touch trade. Its price is voice and standing. An ‘A’-status institution may speak in its own right at the UN Human Rights Council and take full part in GANHRI, with the right to vote and hold office. A ‘B’-status institution may attend, but largely as an observer. The grade measures the independence of an institution, not the human rights record of a nation. Abroad, however, it will be read as both. The world’s most populous democracy, which rightly seeks a seat at the high table, would find its national rights institution seated at the side. Critics would cite it in every forum and each time an Indian diplomat defended the country’s record, the downgrade would be the first footnote in the reply. Strip away the Geneva vocabulary and the stakes are simple. Picture a daily-wage labourer who returns injured from a police station in a district town. His family cannot afford a lawyer and is hundreds of kilometres from the nearest High Court. What it can do is send a complaint to a human rights commission. items.title: UAPA no blanket bar on foreign travel: Delhi High Court allows riots accused Natasha Narwal to go to UK for PhD
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has allowed Delhi riots accused Natasha Narwal to travel to the United Kingdom for academic purposes and to meet her PhD supervisors. Justice Amit Bansal passed the order on October 16 and set aside the trial court order of October 6, which had denied her permission. While passing the order, the Court said that a case under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) will not act as a blanket bar on a person's right to travel abroad. “The fact that the petitioner has been charged of serious offences under the UAPA does not curtail her right to travel abroad in a blanket manner,” the High Court observed in its order. Therefore, the Court allowed her to travel on a personal bond of ₹1 lakh with her brother as surety. Justice Bansal further said she will not seek asylum in the UK or comment on the cases against her. Justice Amit Bansal Narwal is pursuing PhD from University of Warwick and sought permission to attend an international academic conference in London, where her research paper, Gendered Carceral Labour as Social Reproduction, has been accepted for presentation. She also sought permission to meet her PhD supervisors and participate in academic activities at the university. The State opposed her request, arguing that she could pursue her academic engagements via video conference and that travelling to UK could pose difficulties if she seeks asylum there. After considering the case, the High Court noted that Narwal had been pursuing her doctorate remotely since her admission in October 2023 and that her supervisors had specifically invited her for in-person meetings, doctoral training and research activities. The Court observed that the trials were likely to take considerable time to conclude and that there was no allegation that she had violated any bail conditions since being granted bail. Therefore, it allowed her request to travel. Advocates Adit S Pujari, Chaitanya Sundriyal, Manvender Singh Shekhawat and Harshvardhan Pushkin Sharma appeared for Natasha Narwal. Additional Solicitor General (ASG) SV Raju , Special Public Prosecutors (SPP) Madhukar Pandey and Ayodhya Prasad with advocates Dhruv Pande, Aarush Bhatia, Saravjeet Singh and Ishika Singla represented the Delhi Police. items.title: Mini Cooper crash: Kerala court denies bail to accused Suhail Sajeev and 3 others
items.summary: A Kerala court on Saturday denied bail to Suhail Sajeev and three others, booked in connection with the Mini Cooper car accident which led to the death of three motorcyclists. Sajeev along with Ninav, Joel and Ameer had filed bail applications before a trial court in Angamaly. However, Judicial First Class Magistrate Samyuktha MK dismissed their bail pleas. The case stemmed from an accident which happened on October 11 when a Mini Cooper driven by Sajeev at high speed hit a scooter carrying three youngsters on the Athani-Airport Road in Nedumbassery, killing all three. According to the First Information Report (FIR), the impact threw all three onto the road, causing severe injuries to their heads and bodies. While two of them died on the spot, the third succumbed to injuries later. The Nedumbassery Airport Police Station registered a case under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The police subsequently arrested Sajeev and three others in connection with the incident. The three were riding in the car along with Sajeev, who was behind the wheel. All four accused were remanded to 14 days of judicial custody on October 14. According to reports , Sajeev was driving under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. During the bail hearing on October 16, the counsel appearing for the accused argued that the incident only amounted to rash and negligent driving rather than culpable homicide. It was also argued that the victims too had violated the traffic rules as all three of them were riding on a scooter while using the middle lane of the road. The abetment charges against the other three accused were challenged on the ground that they had only accompanied Sajeev in the car. However, the prosecution and the victim's counsel opposed the bail plea, arguing that the accident could not be treated as an ordinary case of negligent driving. CCTV footage was relied upon to show that all the accused had visited several bars and were inebriated before the accident. It was also alleged that the co-accused in the car had encouraged Sajeev to drive, despite knowing that he was drunk. The Court today dismissed the bail pleas. Advocates Saiby Jose Kidangoor, Sreeraj S Rajaram and Afsana Khan appeared for Sajeev.

items.title: Another rape, another suo motu cognizance, but what happens after?
items.summary: Recently, the Supreme Court, in a suo motu writ petition In Re: Recent rape incidents in Delhi NCR gave directions on institutional reforms for improving women’s safety in the Delhi-NCR region. The Court’s intervention comes in the aftermath of the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year old minor in Delhi’s Aastha Kunj Park. This is not the first instance the Court has taken suo motu cognizance of a matter concerning women’s safety against sexual violence. In 2024, the Court did the same in the RG Kar case and gave directions for the creation of safer working conditions for medical professionals. While such initiatives from the Court are admirable, a harder question to answer is: what happens after such directions are issued? The Court’s directions, without any corresponding enforcement mechanism, fail to achieve the aim that they are issued with. The suo motu cognizance addresses institutional failure as a common denominator in such instances of crimes against women. Pointing to the same, the Court also commented on how solidarity shown by the authorities is not the answer to this “ social evil ”. The Court’s order accounts for existing preventive measures like the National Database on Sexual Offenders, the Safe City Project and One Stop Centres. It tries to assess their demonstrated efficacy in fulfilling their purpose. In its subsequent order on October 5 , the Court also directed the Delhi Police to set up real-time monitoring cells in addition to CCTV surveillance in public spaces. The two orders by the Court demonstrate a vigorous attack on institutional failure. However, this vigour is bound to fizzle down without attached subsequent action, which is what happened in the 2024 case. In August 2024 , the Court took suo motu cognizance in the case of the rape and murder of a trainee doctor in RG Kar Medical College and proposed the constitution of a National Task Force (NTF). The NTF was tasked with formulating recommendations for enhanced safety and better working conditions for medical professionals. In November 2024 , the NTF submitted its recommendations for better working conditions and prevention of violence (including sexual violence) against medical professionals. items.title: PIL in Calcutta High Court seeks double-side printing on A4 paper for pleadings in West Bengal courts
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Calcutta High Court seeking a uniform mandate for filing physical pleadings and documents in 75 GSM A4 paper in duplex (back-to-back) format in the High Court and other courts across West Bengal [Akash Sharma v. Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta and Another] . The PIL aims to lower paper consumption, printing services and costs and the physical bulk of court records. The case is listed for hearing on November 23. Calcutta High Court on February 22, 2021 had asked its administrative side to consider mandating use of A4 paper with double-side printing for pleadings and filings. However, the plea filed by advocate Akash Sharma states that further progress of the matter could not be ascertained through publicly available records or notices. This PIL primarily seeks to determine the outcome of the order dated February 22, 2021 and a fresh consideration of the matter to prescribe a uniform practice of using 75 GSM A4 paper in a duplex-printed format across all courts in the State.

items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday granted bail to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. The order was passed by a court of the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM). Dipke's legal team confirmed the development. The Court has imposed certain conditions on him. Details are awaited. Dipke and All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora were detained by the Delhi Police on October 16 ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest at Connaught Place. Dipke was picked up near his residence while heading to the protest at Connaught Place while Bora was detained while she was marching from Mandi House. items.title: Delhi High Court imposes costs of ₹1 on Niva Bupa for misusing IP jurisdiction to sue influencer
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently imposed nominal costs of ₹1 on Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited for misusing its Intellectual Property (IP) Division's jurisdiction to sue a social media influencer over posts against the insurance company [Niva Bupa Vs Vishal Rattewal]. Justice Anup J Bhambhani held that merely referring to a company's trademark while criticising its services does not constitute trademark infringement, particularly when the person making such statements is not using the mark in the course of trade. "Since the suit was filed and pressed, this court is of the view that filing of such suit amounts to misuse of the special jurisdiction of this court under the Intellectual Property Division, " the Court observed. They sought removal of the content published on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X, besides an apology, damages of ₹5 crore and litigation costs. The dispute originated from a consumer complaint filed by Neeraj Kumar concerning a medical insurance claim against Niva Bupa. On October 9, 2024, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at Charkhi Dadri in Haryana ruled in favour of Kumar and made certain observations concerning medical insurance companies generally. Niva Bupa alleged that Rattewal subsequently published offensive material about the company based on these proceedings. The insurer also objected to his references to an August 2026 order of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), which barred Niva Bupa from opening new places of business for six months over regulatory violations. Niva Bupa argued that Rattewal was attracting social media engagement by disparaging its services and damaging its reputation and infringing its registered trademark. However, the Court questioned how such allegations constituted trademark infringement under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. It noted that Rattewal was neither engaged in the insurance business nor connected with it. The Court held that merely using a company's name to identify it in allegedly disparaging posts did not constitute use of its trademark in the course of trade. items.title: Supreme Court issues contempt notice to Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle over remarks targeting CJI Kant, judiciary
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued a contempt of court notice to journalist Nikhil Wagle and Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut over their statements concerning Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and judiciary [Supreme Court Bar Association v Nikhil Wagle and Anr] A bench of CJI Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi passed the order on a contempt of court petition moved by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA). The Court asked Wagle and Raut to show-cause why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them. The bench, however, did not accede to a request to summon them. “We are giving a show cause ... as of now we are granting exemption for personal appearance. Let us see,” CJI Kant said. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi CJI Kant remarked that courts have never lagged behind in protecting personal liberty or other rights and thus making such attacks on the institution was deeply unfortunate. Probably the courts have never lagged behind in protecting those rights. And if the same people condemn, criticise, take the courts left and right, it is very unfortunate. Very, very unfortunate." CJI Kant further said, "May better sense prevail. We can only pray." MRPL employees gathered outside the mortuary of a private hospital in Mangaluru, where the post-mortem was conducted. They identified the deceased as Rajesh D'Silva, 42. Rajesh was among 12 persons injured in the incident and had been undergoing treatment at a private hospital. He succumbed to burns on the morning of October 17. A resident of Kana in Idya village, Surathkal, Rajesh had worked at MRPL on a contractual basis for several years. He was unmarried. The fire broke out around noon on September 30 after a rupture in the cold separator, which operates at high pressure, in the Coker Hydrotreater Unit. The charred body of MRPL contract employee Manish Karkada, 30, was found after the fire was doused. MRPL had announced compensation of Rs 1.2 crore to Manish’s family. It also announced health insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh for each MRPL contract employee and his or her family members. The company has informed the stock exchanges, BSE and NSE, that the financial impact of the fire is provisionally estimated at Rs 118.76 crore. CPI(M) Dakshina Kannada district secretary Muneer Katipalla condoled the death and demanded that MRPL pay Rajesh’s family the same amount in compensation as it had to Manish’s family, and provide jobs at MRPL to their family members. He urged that compensation also be paid to residents of villages surrounding MRPL whose properties had been damaged by the intensity of the explosion. Muneer also demanded that the investigation be made public. "The preliminary investigation report into the factors that caused the tragedy must be made public. An inquiry into the explosion must be conducted by a committee that includes representatives of the civil society,” he said . He also demanded that the government abandon MRPL's proposed Phase IV expansion project, citing Mangaluru's carrying capacity and the dense population in the surrounding areas.

items.title: DMK demands Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, return to pre-SIR electoral rolls
items.summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) has demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into his conduct over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. At a meeting chaired by party president MK Stalin in Chennai on October 17, the party adopted four resolutions: Opposition to the SIR, support for protests against it, criticism of the Congress and the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), and a demand for electoral reforms. The DMK accused Gyanesh of overseeing the deletion of eligible voters’ names despite objections from the other two Election Commissioners. “He must be removed and subjected to an appropriate inquiry,” a resolution said. The party also demanded that the SIR be scrapped completely and that future elections be conducted using the electoral rolls prepared before the revision. It said the exercise should protect voters’ rights rather than deprive eligible citizens of their right to vote, and called for adequate time to be provided for adding and deleting names. The DMK said it would submit a representation to President Droupadi Murmu seeking the cancellation of the SIR and a return to paper ballots instead of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). The party argued that alleged discrepancies between EVM counts and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips had raised questions about the credibility of the machines. “That is why the DMK has been demanding the counting of VVPAT slips. People’s faith in elections can be restored only by returning to the paper ballot system,” the party said. Another resolution extended support to student organisations and other groups protesting against the SIR. The party also backed the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protests demanding Gyanesh’s removal and withdrawal of the revision exercise and condemned the police action against young protesters. The DMK also criticised the Congress, accusing it of taking different positions on the SIR depending on the state. It alleged that while the Congress opposed the exercise nationally, it had not taken a similarly strong position in Tamil Nadu and Kerala. “The Congress is intimidated by the impact of the protests. Though it remained an onlooker initially, it came under pressure to join them as they gained momentum. items.title: Bail denied to Kochi Mini Cooper accident accused, tests show high blood alcohol levels
items.summary: The Angamali Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, on October 17, denied bail to the four accused in the Nedumbassery car accident that claimed three lives. First accused Suhail Sajeev (19) who drove the vehicle, and his three friends Ninav (19), Joel (20), and Ameer (20) will continue in judicial custody. Suhail had hit a two wheeler from the back while driving in the early hours of October 11 in Nedumbassery near Kochi. The crash resulted in the deaths of Gopika (22), Iyas (21) and Devika (21) who were part-time workers in an antique shop in Thrikkakara. The accident, a result of Suhail allegedly being drunk and driving rashly, has triggered huge public protests in Angamali. Suhail’s lawyer told the media that an appeal will be filed at a sessions court. While Suhail has been charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, his friends Ninav, Ameer and Joel are facing charges of abetment. The prosecution reportedly submitted evidence, including lab reports of blood and urine tests, showing alcohol use along with CCTV visuals of the accident. Suhail’s blood alcohol level was high at the time of the accident, police have reportedly found. Reports say that the test found 160 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood in Suhail. This is five times the permissible limit of 30 mg per 100 ml. A urine test also reportedly confirmed that Suhail was highly intoxicated at the time of the accident. Ninavu’s blood test also showed that he’d consumed alcohol. Meanwhile, the Motor Vehicle Department has initiated steps to suspend Suhail’s license. The Angamali Regional Transport office has sent a show cause notice to Suhail’s address. The Excise Department has served show cause notices to the establishments that served liquor to 19-year-olds. The Kerala High Court has asked the Excise Department to seek an explanation from them within seven days.

items.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke granted conditional bail, must sign peace bond
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was granted conditional bail on Saturday, October 17, after being detained while heading to a protest in Delhi. Police said he would be released after signing a bond requiring him to maintain peace for one year. Abhijeet was produced before a Special Executive Magistrate after Delhi Police detained him on October 16 evening while he was on his way to the CJP’s ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest at Connaught Place’s Central Park. He was detained shortly after stepping out of a house in the Jhandewalan area where he was staying. Earlier on Friday, police personnel had served Abhijeet a notice prohibiting him from holding the march, citing his public statements and calls on social media to gather at Connaught Place without permission. Despite the notice, he stepped out at around 4.50 pm, wearing a white t-shirt bearing Mahatma Gandhi’s photograph and carrying the national flag. In a video of the detention, Abhijeet can be heard questioning the police, saying, “I am alone. Why are you stopping me?” He then unfurled the tricolour before police personnel pushed him into a van. Police initiated preventive action against Abhijeet under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Section 126 allows an Executive Magistrate to take preventive action against a person considered likely to breach the peace, while Section 170 provides for preventive arrest to stop the commission of a cognisable offence. Abhijeet had previously signed a peace bond undertaking not to disturb public order for one year after Delhi Police took him and CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka into custody from their flight at the Delhi airport on October 10. Police subsequently arrested him in a fresh case over an alleged violation of that undertaking. Saurav and Ashutosh remain in judicial custody after they were detained on allegations of entering the Jantar Mantar area on October 13. A Special Executive Magistrate remanded them to five days of judicial custody over the alleged breach of their peace bonds. All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, who was also detained on Friday while heading towards the protest, was released early on Saturday. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: விசாரணை வளையத்தில் Arun IPS! | CM Vijay | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The investigation into the POCSO cases against businessman R Veeramani has widened, and is raising serious questions now about how the Chennai police handled complaints against him. While the SIT continues to share details about private individuals arrested in the case, the Chennai police appear reluctant to disclose details of the inquiry involving its own officers. With no detailed public statement on the questioning of former Chennai Police Commissioner A Arun and former Additional Commissioner (South) N Kannan, questions remain over the transparency of the probe into the police department’s handling of the case. In this week's episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the latest developments in the Veeramani POCSO case, the questions surrounding the police investigation, and the need for accountability when allegations of serious crimes involve those entitled to enforce the law.
